text: May 2024 and January 2025, the IRS allocated $10 billion in tax credits (worth 30% of eligible project costs) to approximately 250 applicants over two rounds of funding. To date, 59 applicants have self-disclosed their 48C awards, of which three will recycle solar modules, one will produce solar-grade polysilicon, and one will produce solar-grade glass. • The 48D (Advanced Manufacturing Investment Tax Credit) provides a 25% tax credit for purchasing and commissioning property to build a facility whose primary purpose is the manufacturing of semiconductors or semiconductor manufacturing equipment. The United States Treasury released its final rules for 48D in October 2024, in which they clarified that solar wafer manufacturing facilities were eligible for the credit. Shortly after, Norsun signed an agreement with an engineering, procurement, and construction company, Clayco, to build its wafer facility in Oklahoma. Corning also confirmed soon after the final rule release that it would manufacture solar wafers. • In October 2024, the U.S. Department of Commerce announced a $325 million award to Hemlock Semiconductor from the CHIPS Incentives Program to support the construction of a new manufacturing facility that will produce polysilicon for the solar and semiconductor industries. The award was finalized in January 2025. • In December 2024, the DOE Loan Programs Office awarded a $1.45 billion loan guarantee to Qcells to produce ingots, wafers, cells, and finished modules in Georgia. • Since the domestic content bonus credit of Sections 48 and 45 was introduced and a safe harbor table was published that provides clearer pathways to qualification, several manufacturers have announced solar products with higher levels of domestic content to help projects qualify for the bonus. While the domestic content bonus credit is given to electric generation asset owners, not manufacturers, it indirectly supports domestic manufacturing by giving those products and components more value. We evaluated U.S. manufacturers’ ability to supply the various sectors of the 47.1 GW U.S. dc market for PV systems installed in 2024 under the domestic content criteria for Section 48 and 45 tax credits.5 The total U.S. market for PV systems installed during 2024 is shown in Figure ES-4. Domestic content in this figure is defined following the 2024 safe harbor tables and can be split into four system types defined in the IRS document: ground-mount tracking, ground-mount fixed-tilt, rooftop string inverter, and rooftop MLPE. When considering all these system types together, the domestic content is roughly 13.5% by value, in a total market size of $24.1 billion. However, this percentage varies between system types and between individual PV system projects.
